# What is left of SEEN-114, and the exact commands

SEEN-140 is merged (39d6301) and this branch is rebased onto it. The measurement
SEEN-140 existed for was taken before this note was written: `slice_files` on this
ticket's own diff now reads

    PASS: All 101 changed files are named by the accepted slice plan, or are the
    ticket file the procedure itself writes

against the same check naming about forty files as belonging to no slice in each of
the three triages that returned this ticket. The defect is gone. What is left is
bookkeeping.

## State

At tdd, attempt 6, 108 records, `doctor` clean, the journal's chain intact through
the rebase. All four slices are proved in the branch: 22 traceable rules, every
fixture firing, `rule_candidate` on the review gate, the weekly report's four figures
and the doctor warning. The Outcome is written and the criteria are ticked.

Two things the rebase changed that this note is mostly for. The commit restoring
SEEN-139's reverted paragraphs is gone from this branch, dropped as already upstream,
which is what the cherry-pick was for; the Outcome's paragraph about it is corrected
to say so rather than naming a commit a reader would not find. And every check from
attempt 5 is now a citation against a tree that moved, so they cannot be cited.

## The replay, which is all the tdd stage needs

Four slices, each one: put that slice's production files back to the commit before
it, record the red, restore, record the green. Then the regression and the coverage
last, in that order, because the fingerprint check at the triage compares the tree
against the regression's tree and anything committed after it moves the tree.

Pass every command after `--` as separate words. This is zsh, which does not
word-split an unquoted parameter, and this journal already carries seven records at
exit 127 from that mistake.

    C="python3 harness/run.py check SEEN-114 --phase"
    A="--actor claude:implementer --model opus --quiet"

Slice 1, the compiler and Biome. The red command is `./scripts/rules.sh fixtures`.
Put it back with `git checkout 708d6c6 -- tsconfig.base.json` and move `biome.json`
aside; restore with `git checkout HEAD -- tsconfig.base.json` and move it back. Seven
of its eight rules report not firing.

Slice 2, the ground rules. Same command. Move `sgconfig.yml`,
`.dependency-cruiser.json` and `knip.json` aside; all fourteen of its rules report
their configuration absent.

Slice 3, rule_candidate. The red command is
`python3 -m unittest harness.tests.test_gates`. Put the gate back with
`git checkout <the commit before slice 3> -- harness/gates.py`; four of eight cases
fail with `HarnessError not raised`.

Slice 4, the loop back. The red command is `python3 -m unittest` over
`harness.tests.test_calibration harness.tests.test_stage_gates harness.tests.test_hooks
harness.tests.test_report harness.tests.test_doctor harness.tests.test_rules`.
Put back `harness/report.py`, `harness/doctor.py`, `harness/rules.py`,
`harness/cli.py` and the three fixture test files to the commit before slice 4.
Note that `harness.tests.test_triage` was in this red before the rebase and must not
be now: the paragraph it guards is upstream, so reverting this branch's files no
longer makes it fail.

Then `--phase regression` over `python3 -m unittest discover -s harness/tests`, then
`python3 harness/run.py coverage SEEN-114 --actor claude:implementer`, then the tdd
record citing the four new pairs and the new regression.

## After that

`harness review triage SEEN-114`. It returned this ticket three times on criteria 2
and 5 at 0.36 to 0.39 and 0.41 to 0.50, with `slice_files` failing each time. That
check now passes, and criteria 2 and 5 are the two whose evidence lives in the files
it was mislabelling, so the honest expectation is that they score higher. If either
still comes back unevidenced, the evidence is already in the journal and record 103
lists it: 90 is the timed staged run at 614ms, 69 the whole set over the tree, 71
every rule refusing its fixture, 91 and 92 knip clean on core and the connectors by
name, 70 the citation check. Do not record more checks to move a probability.

Then the reviewer subagent on the triage's own task text, the review record, and
delivery: push, open the PR from the template, wait for CI, `verify-delivery`, the
receipt hash into the PR body, `verify-merge`.

## What a reviewer will need pointing at

Record 103 accounts for every check in this journal, which it needs: seven are
misfires at exit 127, three sets of replayed pairs exist of which only the last is
cited, record 15 is a green that exited 1 and record 72 a staged run with nothing
staged. Record 107 explains the three triage returns and the one cause under them,
which was SEEN-140's defect and is now fixed.

Rework stands at two returns on this ticket, both the same mistake: a solution record
that named the files a change is written in and not the files the change makes fail.
